candidate_rule: Each record yields two non-promoted candidates: its verified fact and the explicit source scope guard.

scope_guards.bduk_july26: Rounded monthly contract management information covers initial-scope premises, can lag contract delivery and does not identify current retail orderability or exact UPRNs.
scope_guards.complaints_record_low: Complaint rates and provider rankings are aggregate regulator data and do not establish service quality, faults or availability at an exact address.
scope_guards.switch_2g3g: National switch-off schedules may change and do not prove a device, SIM, roaming arrangement or parcel currently has usable 2G, 4G or 5G service.
scope_guards.mobile_count_on: Policy statements and linked research describe programme aims and study scope; they are not engineering measurements or exact-address connectivity evidence.

The latest Ofcom complaints figures covered January to March 2026.
Broadband complaints fell to six per 100,000 customers in Q1 2026, the lowest level in Ofcom's series.
The comparable broadband complaint rate had peaked at 40 per 100,000 customers in 2011.
Plusnet and TalkTalk were the most complained-about landline providers and both increased quarter on quarter.
EE, Sky, Utility Warehouse, Virgin Media and Vodafone were the least complained-about landline providers.
Sky Mobile generated the most pay-monthly mobile complaints, mainly about changing provider.
EE, Giffgaff, Tesco Mobile, Three and Vodafone generated the fewest pay-monthly mobile complaints.
EE and Virgin Media were the most complained-about pay-TV providers.
EE pay-TV complaints were mainly about complaint handling, while Virgin Media's were mainly about billing, pricing and charges.
Sky and TalkTalk were the least complained-about pay-TV providers.
Vodafone, EE, Three and O2 had all completed their UK 3G network switch-offs by the page's June 2026 update.
UK 2G networks are scheduled to be switched off gradually over the next few years.
Each mobile network operator sets its own 2G switch-off timetable and Ofcom warns timings may change.
EE announced that it would begin switching off its 2G network from May 2029.
VodafoneThree announced that the Vodafone UK 2G network would switch off during 2030.
Three does not operate a 2G network.
O2 announced that it would begin switching off its 2G network in summer 2029.
O2 began withdrawing inbound-roaming access to its 2G network from 1 October 2025.
The Government published a voluntary 2G switch-off charter in March 2026.
All UK mobile network operators committed to switch off 2G by 2033 at the latest.
Devices and services dependent only on 2G or 3G need migration to at least 4G-capable alternatives.
The switch-offs are intended to support wider use of faster and more reliable 4G and 5G networks.
Ofcom published its mobile-connectivity discussion page on 3 June 2026.
Ofcom states that mobile connectivity underpins how people live, work and travel.
The discussion paper says UK mobile connectivity is too often not good enough.
Ofcom links better mobile connectivity with economic growth and digital inclusion.
The paper sets out Ofcom's view of what good mobile connectivity should look like for people and businesses.
The paper examines why current mobile provision falls short.
It considers how recent market changes may help and where further action may be needed.
Ofcom says reliable mobile connectivity requires effort from industry, government, local authorities, landlords and others.
Ofcom said it would provide an update in early 2027 on lessons, priorities and next steps.
Responses to the discussion paper were requested by 5pm on 29 July 2026.
